content.comment_body: When attempting to install [product_name] [version_no] on Windows 8, the installer crashes. This is a documented issue with the InstallAnywhere installer, which is resolved in [version_no] 2012. Unfortunately, the original DVD uses the 2010 installer version, making installation impossible. Compatibility mode on the installer does not provide a solution. Is there an updated installer package available or any alternative method to resolve this?
Try selecting setup.exe, right-clicking, and choosing 'Run as administrator.' Make sure your antivirus is disabled during the installation process.

I have already attempted those steps. The installer issue is well-known, and I am seeking either a workaround or an updated installer. I am also unsure why [company_name] opts for this Java-based installer.
Could you clarify which operating system version you're using?

I'm using x64, but this detail isn't relevant to the solution. I need an updated installer package. InstallAnywhere's Knowledge Base describes this issue: Installer executable fails on Windows 8 with Stack Trace ZeroGu3 Windows DLL failed to load. See [url]

To my understanding, most or all of [product_name] suite is Java-based and includes its own JVM, which may explain their choice. You should contact the [company_name] development team directly to ask whether a workaround or updated installer with the 2012 InstallAnywhere version is available.

I encountered the same installation issue with several new Windows 8 machines. The solution is to use the latest software DVD and manually copy the required program files to the appropriate folder, then create a shortcut for the executable. Downloaded files from the website do not work, even with administrator privileges.
A new release of [product_name] compatible with Windows 8 seems necessary.
To my knowledge, there is no new version. The existing version works, but the installer is not compatible with Windows 8. The DVD contains the full software so you can bypass the installer package.
Interestingly, [product_name] [version_no] works correctly on Windows 8. [company_name], please provide a solution for this issue.

Please refer to the official information from [company_name] at [url]. Immediate release of a new software version upon the arrival of a new Windows version is not always feasible. While users wish to utilize their new computers promptly, it should be recognized that this is industrial software, and patience is important.

Not sure if this has been resolved elsewhere, but I found a workaround myself. Using the install DVD, copy the folder "Application_winXX" (XX for 32/64-bit architecture) from your optical drive to your computer. Then run the executable from your new folder. You can open or create projects, and ensure file extensions are set to open with the proper program. This workaround allows successful operation until an updated installer becomes available. I'm using Windows 8.1 64bit.

Is the entire DVD content too large? I need the software to practice for a school final. Could anyone with the DVD upload the contents to a file-sharing site until the installer issue is fixed? I have searched but only find the non-functional installer. Thank you.
Just a note, student: Behavior in [product_name] simulation can differ quite a lot from using the actual device. For study purposes, it is acceptable.

Thank you for your help. I had the same issue (DVD with licensed [version_no]), followed the suggested steps, and [product_name] [version_no] worked on Windows 11. Registration is necessary to download [version_no]. Regards.
Please post in English. This is an international community and using English will increase your chances of receiving a response. Here is a translation of your post. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience failures when installing [product_name] [version_no] on Windows 8 due to incompatibility between the InstallAnywhere 2010 installer and the operating system. Attempts such as running as administrator or enabling compatibility mode do not solve the issue. The software itself is not officially supported on Windows 8, making installation and usage challenging. A common workaround involves manually copying files from the DVD, indicating significant hurdles in both installation and compatibility.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to be installable and usable on Windows 8 without errors, preferably through an updated installer or official support for the newer operating system.
